title: Binomial names card
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Living things and their habitats (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from science/y6 lesson 10 (Binomial names card (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 10: The five kingdoms and Carl Linnaeus. To understand how living things are grouped into kingdoms and named with two-part names

questions.q: Polar bear: Ursus maritimus. Which word is the genus?
questions.model: The first word is the genus, with a capital letter. The second is the species. So Ursus is the genus.

questions.q: Why do polar bears and brown bears share 'Ursus'?
questions.a: They are closely related (the same genus).

questions.q: Core: Put 10 living things into the five kingdoms: mushroom, moss, earthworm, yeast, penguin, oak, amoeba, bread mould, Lactobacillus (in yoghurt), seaweed.
questions.a: Fungi: mushroom, yeast, bread mould. Plants: moss, oak. Animals: earthworm, penguin. Protoctists: amoeba, seaweed (some classifications). Bacteria: Lactobacillus.
questions.model: Teacher sorts two first: penguin (animal: eats food, moves), moss (plant: green, makes its own food).

questions.q: Extend: Write three facts about Linnaeus's naming system.
questions.a: Two parts; genus then species; same name used worldwide.

questions.q: Stretch: Why are scientific names in Latin rather than English or Arabic?
questions.a: Latin was the shared language of scholars in Europe at the time, so no one country's language was favoured.

questions.q: Big question: how did Linnaeus give every living thing a name scientists everywhere understand?
questions.a: A two-part Latin name: genus and species, used worldwide.
